title: wsutil: Add UTF-8-aware string buffer
description:
The wmem_strbuf_t has a feature to impose a length limit,
typically used to limit the length of item labels in
the protocol tree.

A common problem with Unicode happens where imposing a byte
length limit will truncate a string mid character and produce
strings with encoding errors.

This adds an UTF-8 ware buffer that takes the length parameters
as the number of unicode codepoints and will never truncate
a string on an invalid boundary.

However it does not do validation currently for input.

Fixes #18653.

notes.body:
added 2 commits
  • 7685c095 - wsutil: Add UTF-8-aware string buffer
  • f989c0fd - 802.11: Use UTF-8 aware strbuf
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/8923/diffs?diff_id=539707565&start_sha=a5676331da1afd0d158ff4a59ca38e2cad5cd300)

Is there any reason why somebody would want a string buffer that does *not* ensure that the string contents are, at least, not truncated in the middle of a UTF-8 sequence?

(I.e., is there any reason why anybody would use the existing string buffer routine with a maximum length specified, rather than using the UTF-8 string buffer?)
I don't think it can be ruled out.

added 2 commits
  • ed22b1c8 - wsutil: Add UTF-8-aware string buffer
  • 7f469f1e - 802.11: Use UTF-8 aware strbuf
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/8923/diffs?diff_id=540612444&start_sha=f989c0fd05f9654c07b2dea41c1554b54cbfca3a)

As long as the maximum size of a label in the protocol tree is based on an octet length, I think there is still a case for a string buffer which is UTF-8 aware and doesn't write a partial character, but has a length based on octets. It shouldn't be too difficult to check at the point of finalizing.

Otherwise, you have an issue where your finalized sized string buffer produces a string that still doesn't actually fit in the label, or else you have to allocate a fixed width string with a length multiplied by (worst case) 4 (as glib's `g_utf8_strncpy` requires). (Although I suppose truncating it later isn't the worst.)

`wmem_strbuf_append_unichar` doesn't quite work correctly because it won't append a partial character, but it fails in the case where, e.g., there is only 1 byte of room left, someone tries to append a 2 byte character (which becomes a no-op) and then subsequently a 1 byte character. It will avoid appending half of the 2 byte character, but then will append the 1 byte character, resulting in inaccurate truncation.
A secondary goal is to remove the maximum label length in octets.

Should this be merged? There isn't an immediate use-case.

> A secondary goal is to remove the maximum label length in octets.

"Remove" in favor of "no limit (other than address space and backing store limits)", or "remove" in favor of "have a maximum length in {characters, glyphs, some other alternative to raw octets}"?
Remove in favor of a maximum length in some alternative that will give approximately the same visual length for any string.

@@ -0,0 +1,143 @@
+/*
+ * Wrapper around a Wmem String Buffer to make it UTF-8 aware.
+ * Copyright 2022, João Valverde <j@v6e.pt>
+ *
+ * Wireshark - Network traffic analyzer
+ * By Gerald Combs <gerald@wireshark.org>
+ * Copyright 1998 Gerald Combs
+ *
+ * SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-2.0-or-later
+ */
+
+#ifndef __WMEM_UNIBUF_H__
+#define __WMEM_UNIBUF_H__
+
+#include <wireshark.h>
+
+#ifdef __cplusplus
+extern "C" {
+#endif /* __cplusplus */
+
+/* Holds a wmem-allocated UTF-8 string-buffer.
+ *  len is the length of the string (not counting the null-terminator)
+ *      in code units.
+ */
+
+typedef size_t  wmem_u8len_t;     /* Code unit length */
+
+typedef uint8_t wmem_u8str_t;     /* UTF-8 encoded string. */
+
+struct __u8buf;
+
+typedef struct __u8buf wmem_u8buf_t;
+
+WS_DLL_PUBLIC
+wmem_u8buf_t *
+wmem_u8buf_new_sized(wmem_allocator_t *allocator,
+                      size_t alloc_hint, wmem_u8len_t max_len)
+G_GNUC_MALLOC;
+
+
+#define wmem_u8buf_new_label(ALLOCATOR) \
+    wmem_u8buf_new_sized((ALLOCATOR), 0, ITEM_LABEL_LENGTH)
+
+
+WS_DLL_PUBLIC
+wmem_u8buf_t *
+wmem_u8buf_new(wmem_allocator_t *allocator, const gchar *str)
+G_GNUC_MALLOC;
+
+
+WS_DLL_PUBLIC
+wmem_u8buf_t *
+wmem_u8buf_new_len(wmem_allocator_t *allocator, const gchar *str, wmem_u8len_t codelen)
+G_GNUC_MALLOC;
+
+
+WS_DLL_PUBLIC
+wmem_u8buf_t *
+wmem_u8buf_dup(wmem_allocator_t *allocator, const wmem_u8buf_t *strbuf)
+G_GNUC_MALLOC;
+
+
+WS_DLL_PUBLIC
+void
+wmem_u8buf_append(wmem_u8buf_t *buf, const wmem_u8str_t *str);
+
+
+WS_DLL_PUBLIC
+void
+wmem_u8buf_append_len(wmem_u8buf_t *buf, const wmem_u8str_t *str, wmem_u8len_t append_len);
+
+
+WS_DLL_PUBLIC
+void
+wmem_u8buf_append_printf(wmem_u8buf_t *strbuf, const gchar *format, ...)
+G_GNUC_PRINTF(2, 3);
+
+
+WS_DLL_PUBLIC
+void
+wmem_u8buf_append_vprintf(wmem_u8buf_t *strbuf, const gchar *fmt, va_list ap);
+
+
+WS_DLL_PUBLIC
+void
+wmem_u8buf_append_c(wmem_u8buf_t *strbuf, const gchar c);
+
+
+WS_DLL_PUBLIC
+void
+wmem_u8buf_append_unichar(wmem_u8buf_t *strbuf, const gunichar c);
+
+
+WS_DLL_PUBLIC
+void
+wmem_u8buf_truncate(wmem_u8buf_t *strbuf, const wmem_u8len_t len);
+
+
+WS_DLL_PUBLIC
+const wmem_u8str_t *
+wmem_u8buf_get_str(const wmem_u8buf_t *buf);
+
+
+WS_DLL_PUBLIC
+size_t
+wmem_u8buf_get_bytelen(const wmem_u8buf_t *buf);
+
+
+WS_DLL_PUBLIC
+wmem_u8len_t
+wmem_u8buf_get_codelen(const wmem_u8buf_t *buf);
+
+
+WS_DLL_PUBLIC
+wmem_u8str_t *
+wmem_u8buf_finalize(wmem_u8buf_t *buf);
+
+
+WS_DLL_PUBLIC
+void
+wmem_u8buf_destroy(wmem_u8buf_t *buf);
+
+/**   @}
+ *  @} */
+
+#ifdef __cplusplus
+}
+#endif /* __cplusplus */
+
+#endif /* __WS_UNIBUF_H__ */
